description:
THE GOAL of fz-5xp. Everything else exists to make this writable.

A complete JSON parser and serializer in fz, plus a small query driver, with a
hand-written Elixir twin as the oracle and pinned allocation goldens. ~300-400 lines
across 4-6 modules, against a current ceiling of ~22 executable lines
(behavior/quicksort.fz, the largest real program fz has ever run).

Shape:
  input = "{\"users\":[{\"name\":\"ada\",\"age\":36}]}"
  {:ok, doc} = Json.decode(input)
  dbg(Json.encode(doc))
  dbg(Enum.map(doc["users"], fn u -> u["name"] end))
  dbg(Process.heap_alloc_stats())

Why JSON specifically:
  - self-contained. fz has NO argv, NO stdin, and no way for arbitrary libc calls to
    return bytes -- but a runtime-provided extern CAN return a binary
    (fz_binary_concat proves it). JSON takes an embedded literal and prints.
  - forces the library by demand: scanning -> String + native bitstring dispatch;
    objects -> a real Map; arrays -> Enum builders; numbers -> Integer/Float format;
    errors -> {:ok,_}|{:error,_}, which is the only error idiom fz has (no exceptions).
  - measures BOTH costs. The parser is first-order recursion, where TRMC and owned-cons
    reuse should shine. The query driver is HOF-heavy, where the indirect-call tax
    shows: there is no inliner anywhere, the callable slot is blind at the recursive
    core, and artifact.rs:1081 makes any position reached by two distinct lambdas a
    boxed ValueRef -> CallEdge::Indirect. One program, both signals.
  - round-trip decode(encode(x)) == x is a second oracle independent of stdout.

Acceptance: green on run + interp + build against ONE Elixir-owned golden, plus
allocation goldens that are argued, not merely recorded.

comments.text:
GOAL PROGRAM RUNS, landed at 71cab6c75.

`Json.decode/1` and `Json.encode/1` in src/modules/runtime_library/json.fz,
oracled against Elixir's OWN `JSON` module -- 36 assertions across decode,
encode and round-trip, byte-identical on interp, run and build, with
decode(encode(x)) == x for every value type.

Covers: true/false/null, integers, negatives, fractional numbers, strings with
\" \\ \n \t escapes, arrays, objects, arbitrary nesting, and an error result
for malformed input.

NOT YET, so this stays open:
  * exponent notation in JSON INPUT (1.0e-7). fz source can write it now
    (fz-5xp.39) but the decoder's number grammar does not read it;
  * unicode \u escapes;
  * rejecting trailing garbage inside containers -- the top level rejects it,
    the containers are more permissive than the grammar;
  * allocation goldens on a real workload, which the epic's SIGNAL asks for and
    which fz-5xp.49's map sorting now makes worth measuring.

Everything the plan predicted as a blocker turned out not to be, and everything
that actually blocked was found by writing the program: fz-5xp.52, .6, .48, .15,
and Map.put's typed clause family. Recorded in the commit message.

title: Json.decode/1 and Json.encode/1 -- the goal program
